note: The machine-readable register of the v2 Lexicon. The prose page governs; this artifact distills. scripts/validate.py holds the two in agreement: every term here appears on the page, every term on the page appears here. Gloss is the first sentence of the page definition, not a replacement for it. Version bumps ride the same commit as the vocabulary change they describe.

terms.gloss: The capabilities and their beds: the work members live inside.
The Ground and the shell: the shared substrate beneath the beds and the one frame the surfaces wear, so the beds do not collide.
The verification suites and the probe matrix: the channel by which the system checks that the machine agrees with itself, on every change, without being asked.
The signal loop, which keeps its name because it is already the cybernetic instrument: what is workable, what unblocks the most, what has stalled quietly are exactly the intelligence questions.
Proofs and adoption: the acts that close the loop between the machine's claims and the cooperative's word.
Stop cards: pain routed past everything, straight to attention.
The tally: the reading by which the system knows its own state from its own history.
The unit of record.
The event log admits new rows and refuses everything else.
How a wrong event is handled, since it cannot be erased: a new event is written that compensates for the old one and points back at it.
The reading computed over events: state at any moment is the tally of everything that happened up to it, recomputed and never stored, so any figure traces to the events that produced it.
What a tally produces for a particular reader or purpose.
Each member's share of the cooperative's results, as a tally over capital events.
The record of membership shares, one share of common voting stock per member on admission.
A mark every event carries: real or illustrative.
The identity spine: one row per participant, human or not, across every relationship state.
An agent with an active membership: admitted per the Bylaws, one share, one vote.
Someone on the access track: Community, Co-working, or Guild.
A person whose application has been received and whose membership stands at applied.
The link between a sign-in and an agent row.
The operational hand: manages intake, may record lifecycle transitions, attendance, and read the log the matrix assigns.
A build-protocol word, not a database role: the humans who decide, sign, and govern.
Shorthand in the policy layer for the roles with broad read: director, secretary, treasurer, steward.
The member who stands a gathering.
The two parties of an opportunity.
The second human of a proof attestation: a non-organizer member who demonstrates or witnesses alongside the organizer, because belonging is not self-certified.
A non-human agent with capabilities but no authority: the runtime (Nou) and the session-scoped build agents.

terms.term: direct · a member's word to the instrument
terms.gloss: To give the instrument work as a recorded act.
The plan of the build, as a book of conditions rather than dates.
The unit of work: one complete thing a pair of hands can make in a session, carrying an address, an intent, citations, a readiness condition, a deliverable, an acceptance, and its honest status.
A piece's citable code: SUB-01, B-03, X-02, A-01, G-F.
A prepared ground where ordered pieces grow toward their proof: Belong, Gather, Find, Share, Treasury, Shell, Agency, Lexicon, and the cross-cutting bed.
The bed the beds are made in: the tables, the event log, the tally view, the security floor.
The product-side territory: a member capability described in sentences ("a member can register without asking anyone"), which the beds grow.
The validated file holding every piece and its status; the Almanac reads it, the validator enforces it, and status changes land by commit.

drafted (the document exists and governs) · anticipated (defined, upstream must clear) · open · (blocker) (workable or blocked, the mark names by what) · verified (acceptance demonstrated, marked in the steward's name) · attested (a proof's human act recorded).
A piece's acceptance was demonstrated and an organizer marked it so, with evidence cited.
The human act that closes a bed: members demonstrate the capability live, speak the attestation, and record it.
The act by which an adopted module joins its pieces into the Almanac.
The one shape for stopping: standing in (where), found (what, with citations), the question (the smallest one that unblocks), a default (a proposed answer a busy organizer can approve with a word).
An organizer's answer, written into the ledger where the card stands.
A patron member's recorded request that the instrument take up a piece of work: a brief, a kind (draft, build, survey, answer), and the repositories it may touch.
A Run is one isolated working session serving one Direction.
The two hands on everything a Run makes: Authored-by names the instrument, Directed-by names the member who directed it.

An open blocker with a name instead of a date: Q1 (the public label for the opportunity surface), Q3 (the counting rules), the steward's run-through, the first grant (whether the instrument may hold a scoped authority in the record), and the AGY §15 visibility decision.
The authorship mark on agent commits: Authored-by: build-agent / <address>.

SER (the overview) · PRD (what to build, in member sentences) · BP (how agents and organizers work) · UI (tokens and patterns) · IM (the information model and its laws) · VS (verification: suites and proofs) · AM (who may do what, anchored in the Bylaws).

Specifications that arrive after the series and graft their own pieces into the ledger on adoption: PATRONAGE (Programs, contributions, the allocation sequence) · TREASURY (the movement layer and its two-person discipline) · AGY, Common Agency (a member directs the instrument on the record).
The governing instruments in draft: Bylaws v2.1 and Membership Agreement v2.3, each carrying a verbal board adoption of June 2026 and neither executed, published under /legal/ with commentary.
The bylaws citation a policy carries in its comment: the section that authorizes what the policy does.
The order when texts disagree: law and bylaws → board policy → PRD → IM and AM → BP and VS → piece briefs → code.
The visible human act that turns a draft into a record: a merge, a decision written into the ledger, an attestation spoken and recorded.
The Common Information System: the whole of it.
The thirteen tables, the event log, and the tally view, yielded by the Information Model as migration 0001 and proven through G0, the security floor.

The numbered SQL files that stand the database from zero: 0001 substrate · 0002 policies · 0003 sign_agreement · 0004 export views · 0005 matrix conformance · 0006 notices rail · 0007 the front door · 0008 admissions · 0009 profiles · 0010 the programs view · 0011 agreements typing · 0012 designation · 0013 the scheduling act · 0015 the member's notices · 0016 the rail's wider ear · 0017 the direction rail · 0018 the desk's read.
Row-level security: the database itself decides, row by row, what each asker may see or write.

A database function that runs with its own authority to make several writes one act: sign_agreement() lands the signature and its event atomically; apply_for_membership() is the front door, landing application, membership, and event in one motion for a stranger who holds no permissions at all; give_direction() is the only door a Direction enters by, refusing in the words of the rule that refuses.
Sign-in by email: no passwords anywhere in the system.
The path from an event to a human: a database trigger forwards admission events to a small function that delivers notices.
A deliberate single point of replacement.
The walkaway's food: every table serialized to canonical JSON, each file hashed, and a manifest of those hashes whose own sha256 is THE export SHA.

The proof that the cooperative could leave: export the record, stand fresh infrastructure from the public repository alone, import, re-export, and require SHA equality with the tally exactly reconstructed.
The seven CI checks on every change, by their machinery names: ledger-validate, schema-lint, db-verify, rls-audit, gate-rehearsal, restore-test, style-lint.
The rls-audit's heart: every role tried against every table, each probe citing the Authority Map cell it proves.

The mechanical half of the Proof Book: every member-capability sentence run as a committed, sequential journey in CI, with four personas and every refusal asserted, so the human ceremony never discovers a defect.
/commons/join/ · the front door.
/commons/agreements/ · every agreement that binds you, version and standing marked, with inline signing.
/commons/directory/ · members, each with a profile they alone control.
/commons/gatherings/ · gatherings and their sessions: register, cancel, return; hosts record attendance where the record counts it.
/commons/opportunities/ · open invitations to play, practice, and work.
/intranet/programs/ · Programs as organizing bodies for what stands on the board, each with its purpose, its Coordinator, and how it recognizes work.
/intranet/treasury/ · the governance record of every movement the rules care about.
/intranet/direct/ · where a member gives the instrument work and watches the arc of it.
The three kinds of opportunity, from lightest to weightiest: something for its own sake, something to get better at together, something with stakes and obligations.
An opportunity's lifecycle.
A gathering is the thing (a meetup, a workshop, a meeting) with a host and a governing agreement; sessions are its occurrences in time.
